'''Jose Ochoa Juliano Jr.''' (born October 16, 1932) is a Filipino [[physicist]], nuclear [[chemist]], and [[Hospital Administration|hospital administrator]].

==Early life and education==
Juliano was born on October 16, 1932<ref name="famousfilipino">{{cite web |title=Jose O. Juliano |url=http://www.famousfilipino.com/content/view/59/118/ |accessdate=September 10, 2013 |website=Famous Filipino}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=NAST Members |url=https://members.nast.ph/index.php/list-of-nast-members/details/1/40 |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=[[National Academy of Science and Technology]]}}</ref> in [[Calamba, Laguna|Calamba, Philippines]] to a family of scholars: [[botanist]] father Jose B. Juliano and [[dental surgeon]] mother Teodora Ochoa.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Miranda |first=Gil R. |date=2016-01-08 |title=NOTABLES: Calamba's Wall of Fame |url=https://tagacalamba.wixsite.com/calamba/single-post/2016-1-9-notables-calambas-wall-of-fame |access-date=2025-03-25 |website=calamba |language=en}}</ref> Juliano also had 3 brothers: Bienvenido, Petronilo, and Rogelio.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cichon |first=Melchor F. |date=2012-12-08 |title=Biography: Dr. Rogelio Ochoa Juliano: the Generous Achiever |url=http://biographynotmine.blogspot.com/2012/12/dr-rogelio-ochoa-juliano-generous.html |access-date=2025-03-25 |website=Biography}}</ref> 

Juliano graduated with two [[Bachelor of Science]] degrees in [[agricultural chemistry]] and [[mathematics]] from the [[University of the Philippines Diliman]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jose O. Juliano |url=https://spheres.dost.gov.ph/profiles/699-jose-o-juliano |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=spheres.dost.gov.ph}}</ref> as, both, a member of [[Upsilon Sigma Phi]] and with [[magna cum laude]] honors in 1952.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Manchester International Hol (MIH: Philippines) |url=http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=11500843&ticker=MIH:PM&previousCapId=873840&previousTitle=PHILEX%20MINING%20CORP |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130910205052/http://investing.businessweek.com/research/stocks/people/person.asp?personId=11500843&ticker=MIH:PM&previousCapId=873840&previousTitle=PHILEX%20MINING%20CORP |archive-date=September 10, 2013 |access-date=March 23, 2025 |website=Bloomberg Businessweek |publisher=[[Bloomberg Businessweek]] |language=en}}</ref> 

After completing his [[undergraduate education]], Juliano then moved to the United States to pursue [[graduate studies]]. Juliano graduated with a [[Master of Science]] degree in [[electrochemistry]] and [[chemical engineering]] with an emphasis in sugar technology from [[Louisiana State University]] in 1954,<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Louisiana State University and Agricultural & Mechanical College |author-link=Louisiana State University |date=1954 |title=Gumbo Yearbook, Class of 1954 |url=https://repository.lsu.edu/gumbo/54/ |journal=Gumbo Yearbook |location=Baton Rouge, Louisiana |page=278}}</ref> and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in [[nuclear chemistry]] and [[physics]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley|University of California (n/k/a University of California, Berkeley)]] in 1957.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> His doctoral [[dissertation]] was titled ''Coincidence Nuclear Spectrometry With Applications To [[Europium]]-154 And Europium-155.''

== Career, awards, and Calamba Medical Center ==
Juliano worked as an affiliate for the [[American Nuclear Society]], [[American Physical Society]] and [[American Chemical Society]]. He was awarded the 1st annual Ten Outstanding Young Men (TOYM) award for his participation in the [[nuclear physics]] in 1959.<ref name="famousfilipino" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=TOYM |url=https://jciphilippines.com/our-programs/toym/ |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=JCI Philippines |language=en-US}}</ref> Since 1995 he was a consultant of [[Canlubang]], [[Industrial Estate]] and from 1993 to 2002 worked at the [[National Academy of Science and Technology]]. From 1996 to 1998 he worked as undersecretary for international relations, Department of Trade and Industry and by 1999 became a president and CEO of the [[Calamba Medical Center]] board.<ref name=":2" /> During his tenure as president, Juliano teamed up with "chair Efren Recto in convincing the erstwhile conservative directors to start relying on bank loans for expansion" of the medical center which resulted in "the construction of a couple of building annexes."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Yuson |first=Alfred A. |date=July 29, 2019 |title=A center with a history |url=https://qa.philstar.com/lifestyle/arts-and-culture/2019/07/29/1938656/center-history |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Philstar.com |publisher=[[The Philippine Star]] |language=en |publication-place=Manila}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tomandao |first=Roy |date=2019-07-22 |title=Calamba Medical hits 30th year with new buildings |url=https://manilastandard.net/mobile/article/300458 |access-date=2025-03-24 |website=Manila Standard |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Juliano is married to Victoria Juliano (née Galang). The couple have three children together, all of whom have medical careers: Jose Enrico (son), Joji (daughter), and Catherine (daughter).<ref name=":1" />
